descriptor: Operating company · reported in GBP · quoted in GBp (pence)

kpis.label: Net Debt incl. Leases
kpis.change: last disclosed H1 FY2025; company stopped publishing it

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Company FCF (lease-adjusted)
charts.annotation: Owner FCF (DCF card above) further deducts SBC and interest income. Company FCF is Kingfisher's own post-lease-principal-and-interest measure, disclosed only through H1 FY2025; the gap afterwards is the company dropping the disclosure, not a zero.

charts.title: Cash vs Total Debt vs Net Debt incl. Leases
charts.annotation: Total debt excludes IFRS 16 lease liabilities, matching the DCF's net-cash bridge. Net debt incl. leases is Kingfisher's own wider measure (c.GBP 2.2bn of lease liabilities at H1 FY2025); the company stopped publishing it after H1 FY2025.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Kingfisher plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash, debt and lease-adjusted net debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (bank loans, overdrafts and derivatives -- IFRS 16 lease liabilities excluded). Net debt incl. leases is Kingfisher's own wider measure, adding back c.GBP 2.2bn of store lease liabilities.

For Kingfisher plc: the DCF deliberately values the business on net CASH of c.GBP 309m (cash and short-term deposits less bank debt), treating the full lease cash cost as an operating expense inside EBITDA instead of as debt. The wider measure is the one the company itself quotes as "net debt" and is roughly GBP 1.9-2.4bn -- this chart is the reconciliation between the two views, not a contradiction.

What to watch:

  • Whether lease liabilities are shrinking (store closures/renegotiation) or rebuilding
  • That the company stopped disclosing the lease-inclusive figure after H1 FY2025 -- a gap in this series is a reporting change, not improvement

leaseInterest.title: Lease interest paid
leaseInterest.content:
The finance-cost component of IFRS 16 lease accounting: interest on the discounted store lease liability, separate from the lease principal repayment shown in the cash-flow chart.

For Kingfisher plc: the DCF adds lease interest and lease principal back into the owner-FCF bridge (treatment B) because it charges the full lease cash cost through EBITDA rather than splitting it into a financing-style interest/principal split. This chart shows the size of that add-back directly from the cash flow statement.

What to watch:

  • A declining trend (GBP 165m FY2020 to GBP 118m FY2026) as the lease book amortises and the estate rationalises
  • Interest paid versus principal paid -- a shrinking interest share as leases age

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Kingfisher plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Kingfisher plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Company FCF is Kingfisher's own measure, additionally deducting IFRS 16 lease principal and lease interest. Owner FCF (the DCF card above) goes further again, also stripping stock-based compensation and interest income -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Kingfisher plc: store leases are the single biggest adjustment between the three measures -- about GBP 0.5bn/yr of principal plus interest. The company only disclosed Company FCF at the half-year mark through H1 FY2025; its absence afterward is a reporting gap, not a worsening number.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF
  • How much of the net-income-to-FCF gap is lease cash cost versus genuine earnings quality

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Kingfisher plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Kingfisher plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Kingfisher plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Kingfisher plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Kingfisher plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
